heading: ### Gate/probe registry

notes: Verdict-label compression, exit codes and classes correct: row 1's verdict map reads '0 clean; 1 failed; 2 and 64 could-not-evaluate'. The tool's EXIT_BY_ID (tools/repeat-control.py:122-130) is controls_match 0, controls_mismatch 1, baseline_nonzero 2, command_unavailable 2, snapshot_tampered 2, setup_error 2, invalid_usage 64, and the tool's own docstring (lines 43-46) classes all of 2 and 64 as could-not-evaluate. '0 clean; 1 failed' reads as the gate passing or failing, while the tool's finding IDs are controls_match / controls_mismatch; the neighboring round-21 registry row (SKILL.md:2199) writes the same two exits with the IDs attached ('0 clean (controls_match); 1 failed (controls_mismatch)'). Not false, and the exit codes are right; attaching the IDs would remove the ambiguity for a reader who has not opened the tool. (Same observation class as round-27 Read25 M1 and round-27 ReRead08 M3, both recorded as minor gaps, not wrong expectations.)

Round-12 table cell vs the round-21 registry cell use different evidence-file lists for the same tool: row 2's 'Pinned values' cell names declaration.json, declared.tsv and manifest.json, while the round-21 row (SKILL.md:2185) names declaration.json, declared.tsv, summary.json, manifest.json and tools/mutate-and-run.sh with per-file annotations. Both are true of the tree (all five exist at C0); the round-12 cell is the shorter of the two and does not annotate what each pin covers. A reader needing the target/spec/summary/runner pins must read the round-21 row or declaration.json. The same cell lists manifest.json under 'Pinned values' while the section's own prose says 'manifest.json itself is not pinned' - the two are reconcilable only if 'Pinned values' is read as 'the artifacts the probe verifies' rather than 'artifacts whose own digest is pinned'; the prose states the reconciliation explicitly, and the tool confirms it (check excludes manifest.json from its own file set, tools/bash-witness-study.py:840-841, and grep finds manifest.json's own sha256 nowhere under .ufo/evidence/round-12/). Naming the column 'artifacts verified' would close the tension without a text change.

Ordinal is a snapshot, not a live count: 'The bash study deepens one recorded case, never a seventh independently measured gate' is true at C0 in substance (the study is a probe over the already-recorded leg 2, bash-surface-census, B1-B10 - declaration.json pins target fecee8743e52eb8fb5fbb40782934cb619a1a96e and the ten spec defects; tools/registry.json carries it as kind=probe, not a leg), but 'seventh' counts the round-12 six-leg registry. The runner now carries ten legs (SKILL.md:1345, 1432; tools/mutate-and-run.sh:88-97) and SKILL.md elsewhere has a 'seventh recorded case' (lines 1598, 1799). Time-scoping the ordinal ('never a seventh, in the six-leg registry of this write') would prevent a C0 reader from reading it as a live count.

'seat ReRead08' is cited without a path while 'seat Read25' carries one (.ufo/waves/round-27/w1/Read25.md). The ReRead08 report resolves uniquely - .ufo/waves/round-27/residual/ReRead08.md is the only file by that name in the tree - so the citation is locatable, but a path would make it so without a search.

The runner-pin staleness the section discloses is still live at C0, not merely historical: the paragraph says the pin 'is stale at round 27' and the parenthetical exit contract ('check exits 1 DRIFT; run/rerun refuse, exit 2; count never reads the runner') holds verbatim at C0 - check exits 1 with WITNESS_CHECK: DRIFT (observed sha256=977de470... vs committed=75ed934d...), run and rerun exit 2 with CANNOT-EVALUATE (runner-drift), and count exits 0 while the runner is drifted. The 'at round 27' qualifier marks first observation; the drift persists.

The section's own disclosure - 'Witness declarations are integrity-frozen (declaration, mapping, target, spec, summary; manifest.json itself is not pinned)' - is corroborated by the tree and by the round-21 registry's own cell wording; the frozen set excludes the runner, and the runner is separately and correctly named as stale, so no internal contradiction. summary.json's freeze is inherited from manifest.json (sha256 acc01268... appears in manifest.json and matches the file on disk), which is why the manifest's non-self-pin is stated in the same parenthetical rather than left implicit.

Cross-section consistency checked: the round-21 registry row for the same probe (SKILL.md:2185) names 'check' as its entry command with the same exit classes and the same selftest line (WITNESS_SELFTEST: 51/51 pass), while this round-12 row names 'count'; both are live modes of the same tool and both were exercised here. The two rows differ in the exit-64 label ('64 usage only (argparse)' here, '64 could-not-evaluate (usage)' at line 2185); the tool's own docstring settles it - 'Usage errors exit 64 (the probe contract), not argparse's default 2' - so this row's wording is the precise one and the round-21 row's is the loose one. That difference lives in the round-21 row, not in this section.

The calibration correction resolves against the tree: at the round-12 landing commit 9df9212, SHONEN.md line 9 reads '- [~] Instructions executable by an agent without oral context' with the scope-bounded qualifier 'fleet round-1 cold-read of blob 4eb4cf3:SKILL.md - Appendix A + B sweep recipe only' on the following line; immediately before c7986cd the same line read '- [ ]', and c7986cd is an ancestor of 9df9212, so the section's 'carried a scope-bounded [~] at round 12, not [ ]' is exact. corpus/lessons/round-1-verifier-spotcheck.md states the non-credit ('the box-3 increment is not credited (cold-read covered Appendix A+B only, probes reconstructed)'), and the promotion paragraph above (SKILL.md:1514) plus the errata row (SKILL.md:1779) are consistent with it - no contradiction across sections.
